0 to 1 · Project 01

D2D Dealer Order Platform

1,600+ German dealers, fewer than 10 reps, one ERP-integrated portal.

ERP-INTEGRATED ORDERING · GERMANY MVP · 10-MARKET EXPANSION APPROVED

PRODUCTION CAPTURES · GERMANY DEALER PORTAL

Jaehyun Han · Portfolio04
D2D · Problem

The brief blamed communication.
The system did not exist.

1,600+ German dealers were served by fewer than 10 reps. All orders went through an order desk by phone and spreadsheet: 100% of volume, now only 18% for exceptions. Order-to-ERP entry took 3.8 days, and 53% of accounts were sub-$100K, too small to justify manual handling at that pace.

12 dealer visits (n=5) · Germany field research

Jaehyun Han · Portfolio05
D2D · Solution

A new layer plugs into existing ERP.

The dealer portal is a new ordering layer, not a replacement. It sits between dealers and the enterprise ERP/WMS stack that already runs fulfillment, passing structured orders through instead of routing them through people.

Germany MVP 2024.09 · full rollout 2025.01 · TW·MY·MX·ID 2025 · 10-country expansion approved next

Jaehyun Han · Portfolio06
D2D · Results

Order desk load fell, delivery got faster

1,600+ German dealers had routed every order through a phone-and-spreadsheet desk. The ERP-integrated portal cut that queue to exception handling only, and cancellations fell as ERP validation ran in real time instead of by hand. The workflow now runs unattended for ordinary orders; the order desk exists for the exceptions that still need a person.

6.3 → 9.8 items per order 42% → 71% truck load (CBM) 100 → 77 delivery cost index (−23%)
What remained unresolved. About half of subsidiaries still ran parallel spreadsheets six months after launch (estimated). Truck-load and cost gains are Germany-only; the approved 10-market expansion has not launched.

Rollout

Germany went ordering-only in September 2024, then ERP-connected at full scale four months later. The same portal is now approved for Taiwan, Malaysia, Mexico, and Indonesia, with a 10-market expansion next.

22% → 7%Cancellation rate · Observed
8.9 → 4.8dDelivery lead time · Observed
100% → 18%Order desk volume · Observed

Jaehyun Han · Portfolio10
Partner Center · Results

A shared workspace surfaced the next constraint

10+ interviews had shown four surfaces, three re-entries, and zero shared records for a single order. Phase 1 replaced that with one workspace: order management, self-service onboarding, and an open API. By June, 20 of 30 onboarded partners had logged in, representing 88.8% of outbound sales. Coverage is not causation, and cancellation and response-time targets still need a baseline.

1 to 100 · Rewiring workflows

One pipeline now owns every string

Bunjang Global · Product Manager
2026

Background

  1. No owner for product strings
  2. PM drafts copy, designer finalizes text
  3. Handoff passed to frontend by hand
  4. Frontend hardcodes strings per screen

Problem

No shared store meant strings lived wherever someone placed them.

No owner, no store: Japanese would not scale (estimated)

Approach

  1. Figma plugin selects key frames
  2. n8n splits key, text, page id
  3. Lokalise holds the source of truth
  4. Slack requests translation per key link
  5. Figma regenerates keys and frames
Results
Lesson
  1. Translation CTR 44% to 62.2% (Q1 to Q2)
  2. Add-to-cart 31% to 44.3% (Q1 to Q2)
  3. Organic search +27% (Q1 to Q2)
Rank exposed the gap, not the country Japan ranked 6th in traffic and 10th in GMV, but 16th of 16 markets in translation clicks and cart adds. A shared string source closed that gap.
Jaehyun Han · Portfolio16
1 to 100 · Global Business Invoice Automation

33 monthly invoice requests, down to zero

LG Electronics · Product Manager
2024.11-2025.07

Background

  1. No business-invoice function existed
  2. Tax and refund rules differ per country
  3. No ERP-to-OMS field mapping
  4. Subsidiaries emailed ERP by hand

Problem

Ops ticket, then manual dev work, then ERP review. No mapping meant the chain stayed manual.

33 requests / month × 5 hours
= 165 hours (~21 MD)

Approach

  1. 4-country tax-team interviews
  2. Shared fields first, local last
  3. ERP-to-OMS map as the spec
  4. E2E test, then tax-team sign-off
Results
33 manual requests/month -> 0; new country = add fields + mapping.
Lesson
Stable rollout required tax, engineering, and ERP to own one mapping table.
